findings.detail: elite_yellow ("Slabjaw") is given a PANEL's flavour, not a creature's: "Ripped off something that would not lie down. Bolted on, it keeps you upright a beat longer than you deserve." That is verbatim the guard-panel line also used on panel_yellow_guard, panel_red_guard and panel_grey_guard. Slabjaw is a living territorial elite that holds ground and winds up to pounce (§2.7, §2.2); a panel is the thing you strip off it and bolt to your body (§2.8 -- "Elite creatures drop decorated meat panels"). Correction: author Slabjaw fresh flavour describing the animal (a thick-necked ground-holder that will not be moved) and leave the "bolted on / keeps you upright" register to the panels it drops.

All five Grey Alphas carry the common-prey flavour "Doesn't have a specialty because it doesn't need one. Toughest common meal on the menu." An Alpha is the biome's champion, "your equal in rank but fighting at Clash intensity", the hardest fight in the biome and the thing that "cannot be outrun" (§2.5); Clash meat "never wanders at all" and is carried only by elites, minibosses and Alphas (§2.7). Calling one a "common meal on the menu" flatly contradicts its tier and role. Correction: give the Grey Alphas Clash-register flavour of their own (all-round dominance, the thing the biome emptied out for) and keep "toughest common meal" on prey_grey_* where it belongs.

Ridgeripper's arena is written as "A rocky outcrop on high ground, exposed and cramped, with little room to circle wide" -- i.e. the Claws carrier is staged inside the terrain Claws exist to unlock ("Claws | The crag-holder, on rocky outcrops | Climb high ground", §2.6), which the generator is explicitly forbidden to do: "Every trait gate in a biome has a reachable carrier for its trait, outside the terrain that trait unlocks" (§3.3, invariant 1). It also contradicts the biome file, which correctly places the fight at "A boulder-field at the foot of the rocky outcrop ... ground any player can walk into, no climbing required" (biomes.mountains). Correction: rewrite the arena as the boulder-field/approach at the base of the outcrop, with the crag-holder dropping down into it -- reachable with no Claws.

These panels grant powers the game does not have. §2.8 states the panel power set: "Each grants a power: a longer lock range, a stronger dash, a tougher guard, brief camouflage." "vigour" (a health/stamina power -- "Keeps you standing when everything else wants to quit", "yours doesn't quit as fast") and "bite" (a damage power -- "Wear it on your fist and let it finish the sentence") are invented mechanics. Worse, "wear it on your fist" implies a punch attack; the only offensive verb in the game is lock -> pounce -> knock down -> eat (§2.1). Correction: re-power these five panels onto the four stated powers (lock_range, dash_power, guard, camouflage) and rewrite their flavour to describe those effects.

Two distinct panels ship under one name: both panel_blue_lock_range and panel_grey_lock_range are called "Dead-Eye Socket" (with different flavour and different attach points). The shared data contract gives each panel its own authored name and magnitude in `panels.json` (§3.3), and the game must show the player two panels side by side to choose between when at capacity ("you pick which to shed, both powers shown", §2.8) -- identical names make that screen unreadable, and lock_range panels are exactly the pair most likely to be compared. Correction: rename one of them (e.g. keep "Dead-Eye Socket" on the Blue drop, rename the Grey drop).

"Old Grey's Second Wind Gland" attributes the panel to "Old Grey" -- which is the authored name of the Grey Alphas in this very content set (alpha_prairies_grey "Old Grey of the Tall Grass", etc.). §2.8 pins the source of panels: "Elite creatures only. Never grazers, never ordinary prey, never the four trait minibosses" -- and what you take off an Alpha is the emblem, a trophy that grants no power (§2.5). Naming a panel after the Alpha says a panel dropped off an Alpha. Correction: name it off its actual dropper, elite_grey ("Greybrute"), or use a non-Alpha descriptor.

The Fins pocket reads "Old Gillmaw holds the mudbank there" -- but the Fins trait miniboss in the creature roster is named "Gillbrute" (miniboss_fins). No creature called Old Gillmaw exists. The other four pockets correctly refer to their carriers by the GDD's own descriptors ("the crag-holder", "the shaggy grazer-hunter", "the vent-dweller", §2.6); this one invents a proper name and breaks referential integrity between `biomes.json` and `creatures.json` (§3.3 -- schema/reference checks on static data). Correction: say "Gillbrute" or "the pond-dweller".

All five grazers ship byte-identical idle and when_locked text ("Stands and grazes in place, calm and limbless ... no colour, no watchfulness, nothing to lose" / "Freezes for a single beat ... never turning to fight"). The rules content is correct -- no colour, limbless, never fights, bolts on lock (§2.3, §2.2) -- but five identical paragraphs read as one entry pasted five times. Tighten with a per-biome verb (wading, floundering in ash) while keeping the same three facts.

"Pale meat that survives the heat by being too dumb to notice it." Grazers are white -- "the same white as a bare limb and a newborn cube" (§2.3) -- and "Pale" is the name of a wild intensity tier (§2.4b). Capitalised at the head of the line it can misread as the tier. Prefer "White meat" or "Colourless meat".

Each family's flavour is reused verbatim across all four tiers and then again on that family's five Alphas -- twenty prey entries and twenty-five Alphas carrying five lines between them. Nothing is contradicted, but the Bestiary is read comparatively, side by side (§2.9), so a Rage Chugger and a Pale Chugger reading identically wastes the one place the game has a voice. Vary at least the tier extremes.

"Blink and it's already gone -- or already biting." sits awkwardly against the entry's own when_locked ("Explodes away in a blur of frantic, tight zig-zags ... just to panic") and against Red's stat identity, "weakest bite" (§2.4). Same note on the Yellow line's "Hits like a slammed door". Not a contradiction -- same-rank creatures do hunt you (§2.2, §3.3) -- but the bite brag undercuts the flight behaviour it is printed next to.

"Toughest common meal on the menu" -- Grey is the family whose "meat runs rarest" (§2.4), so "common" is the one word in the line that fights the family's stated scarcity. "Toughest meal on the menu" fixes it without losing the joke.

The Red Alpha's emergence -- "a streak of colour where a moment ago there was only bones and scorched ground" -- is biome-blind: the Wetlands lair is "A drowned hummock deep in the marsh, black water lapping at a ring of picked-clean bones" and the Mountains lair is frost-cracked stone. Scorched ground belongs to the Prairies mound and the Volcanic rim. Swap the last clause per biome.

"The Last Grey" ships the Grey Alpha's behaviour text word for word ("The den collapses open and it simply walks out ..."). The Apex is the world's ultimate, a rank-6 Clash creature and "your final mirror" (Ascension section) -- it should not read as one more biome champion. Also, the name's implication of a last-of-its-kind edges toward backstory the game does not have; the flavour "Woke up because you wouldn't stop eating" is the right register and does the job alone.

"Overclocked Heart" -- "overclocked" is machine-shop/computing register in a game whose voice brief is "primal, crude, comedic" (§3, Content & Tone Agent). "Burst Heart", "Blown Heart" or similar keeps the joke inside the game's mouth.
"Knucklebone Knuckle-Wrap" stutters -- knuckle twice in three words. Tighten (e.g. "Jawbone Knuckle-Wrap"), which also matches its own flavour, "Somebody's jawbone, still shaped like a jaw."

The attach string "temple ridge, off the main face" leaks the spec into the fiction -- the rule (panels never crowd the main-face traits, §2.8/§2.6a) is being obeyed correctly, but the player-facing text should just say where it sits, not cite the constraint. Drop "off the main face".

All three guard panels share one flavour line: "Ripped off something that would not lie down. Bolted on, it keeps you upright a beat longer than you deserve." Three elites, three different animals -- give each its own; the Grey one especially, since Greybrute is the rarest dropper.

"Nightcrawler's Hind Haunch" credits a creature not in the roster -- the Purple elite that drops it is "Backbiter" (elite_purple). Poetic rather than broken, but the panel names elsewhere point at real droppers; prefer Backbiter or an unnamed descriptor.

"Strap it under your skin" hides a panel that is supposed to be visible: panels "visibly attach to your body -- you can see how much you've eaten by looking at yourself", and the silhouette is the inventory screen (§2.8). "Strap it over your skin" or "lash it on" preserves the read.

These attach to limbs -- "strapped across the forearm, over the knuckles", "hind leg joint", "rear haunch". §2.8 places panels "anywhere across the cube's faces, wherever the authored body plan leaves room", and §2.6a is emphatic that limbs are the colour system's real estate and the two systems "never compete for the same real estate". No stated rule is broken, but body-face wording (flank, hump, shoulder) is safer and matches the rest of the set.

Every entrance line uses the same construction -- "grazes soft and Pale" / "still graze soft" -- five times over. It also blurs two things the game keeps apart: grazers (white, no colour, healing) and the Pale tier of coloured prey (§2.3, §2.4b). Reword so the entrance says which one is thick on the ground.

The terrain line claims "the only biome whose deep end runs Rage from edge to edge", but its own deep_end says "Deep and Rage wander together out here", and Beach's deep_end already runs "Deep and Rage ... the full ladder loose on open ground" -- Rage wanders the deep ends of both Beach and Volcanic (§2.4b). Not false about the danger, just over-claimed as unique; soften to the hardest ground rather than the only Rage ground.
